replicated_originals.reference: Reed, John Shelton (1972) The Enduring South: Subcultural Persistence in Mass Society (pp. 26-29; the 1970 UNC regional-stereotype study)

A.reason: The abstract and text say the 1970 study reported in Reed (1972, pp. 26-29), on southern students' stereotypes of white southerners, white northerners and Americans, 'was replicated in 1987'. This is a self-replication, which the codebook counts. The candidate is a 1972 Heath book, but its DOI is a JSTOR 10.2307 DOI, which probably belongs to a journal item such as a book review, not to the book itself.

B.reason: Katz and Braly (1933) supplied the 84-adjective trait-list instrument and the 'definiteness' index. Their findings on stereotypes of ethnic and national groups are not re-tested: the paper studies regional groups and compares against the 1970 Reed study.

notes: The paper spells the name 'Braley'. Footnote 4 says the 1970 study also asked about the Katz-Braly groups, but the 1987 study asked only about three groups (white southerners, white northerners, Americans), so the Katz-Braly targets were not replicated.
